theory.intro: When adding or subtracting numbers with different numbers of digits, line them up by place value so each column holds ones, tens, hundreds and so on. You can also add by grouping matching place-value parts.
facts: **Align the place values** (ones under ones, tens under tens) — line up the right-hand ends for whole numbers.
Add a column at a time, **regrouping** into the next column when the total reaches $10$ or more.
When adding three or more numbers, a column total can be larger than $19$ — carry the full tens part, including any amount carried from the previous column.
Empty places act like a $0$.

When subtracting, regroup if the top digit is smaller than the digit being subtracted. Exchange $1$ unit of the next place for $10$ units of the current place. If the next place contains $0$, regroup from a higher place first.
For a subtraction with three or more numbers, subtract the second number from the first, then subtract each remaining number from the running result in order.
For addition by partitioning, split each number into place-value parts, group equal places, add the groups and combine their totals.
In a calculation with both addition and subtraction, work through the operations from left to right, using the running result.
steps: Choose the required operation. For column working, align equal place values. For addition by partitioning, group matching place-value parts.

For column working, work from ones towards higher places. Include carried amounts when adding; exchange higher-place units when subtracting. For partitioning, add the matching groups and combine their totals.
For repeated subtraction or mixed addition and subtraction, use the running result for each next operation in written order.

theory.intro: When adding or subtracting numbers with different numbers of digits, line them up by place value so each column holds ones, tens, hundreds and so on. You can also add by grouping matching place-value parts.
facts: **Align the place values** (ones under ones, tens under tens) — line up the right-hand ends for whole numbers.
Add a column at a time, **regrouping** into the next column when the total reaches $10$ or more.
When adding three or more numbers, a column total can be larger than $19$ — carry the full tens part, including any amount carried from the previous column.
Empty places act like a $0$.

When subtracting, regroup if the top digit is smaller than the digit being subtracted. Exchange $1$ unit of the next place for $10$ units of the current place. If the next place contains $0$, regroup from a higher place first.
For a subtraction with three or more numbers, subtract the second number from the first, then subtract each remaining number from the running result in order.
For addition by partitioning, split each number into place-value parts, group equal places, add the groups and combine their totals.
In a calculation with both addition and subtraction, work through the operations from left to right, using the running result.
steps: Choose the required operation. For column working, align equal place values. For addition by partitioning, group matching place-value parts.

For column working, work from ones towards higher places. Include carried amounts when adding; exchange higher-place units when subtracting. For partitioning, add the matching groups and combine their totals.
For repeated subtraction or mixed addition and subtraction, use the running result for each next operation in written order.

||

|column.|

- Regroup numbers in different forms (Reasons about quantity)

||

+------------------------------------------------------------------+

- Partition numbers to 1 billion in non-standard forms

+------------------------------------------------------------------+

|$$150\ 000 + 13\ 480$$, so that 150 000 could then be doubled|
|and added to 13 480.|
||

theory.intro: When adding or subtracting numbers with different numbers of digits, line them up by place value so each column holds ones, tens, hundreds and so on. You can also add by grouping matching place-value parts.
facts: **Align the place values** (ones under ones, tens under tens) — line up the right-hand ends for whole numbers.
Add a column at a time, **regrouping** into the next column when the total reaches $10$ or more.
When adding three or more numbers, a column total can be larger than $19$ — carry the full tens part, including any amount carried from the previous column.
Empty places act like a $0$.

When subtracting, regroup if the top digit is smaller than the digit being subtracted. Exchange $1$ unit of the next place for $10$ units of the current place. If the next place contains $0$, regroup from a higher place first.
For a subtraction with three or more numbers, subtract the second number from the first, then subtract each remaining number from the running result in order.
For addition by partitioning, split each number into place-value parts, group equal places, add the groups and combine their totals.
In a calculation with both addition and subtraction, work through the operations from left to right, using the running result.
steps: Choose the required operation. For column working, align equal place values. For addition by partitioning, group matching place-value parts.

For column working, work from ones towards higher places. Include carried amounts when adding; exchange higher-place units when subtracting. For partitioning, add the matching groups and combine their totals.
For repeated subtraction or mixed addition and subtraction, use the running result for each next operation in written order.
